title: Adjust LOD selection metrics to use attribute error
body:
This change intends to improve LOD selection or, to be more precise, to make it attribute aware such that the LODs that preserve the shape well but preserve attributes poorly are selected at a further distance cutoff. Mechanically, the change is pretty simple and mostly involves reverting the meshoptimizer patch that stayed with Godot since before the attribute metric was functioning properly, and adjusting a few constants:

- Revert meshoptimizer patch; the metric used for LOD selection now incorporates attribute error
- Since LOD selection is now aware of attribute deviation, we don't need to use a higher normal weight
- To prevent normal creases from creating input triangles with very large normal deviation, reduce default normal merge threshold
- Since we now use combined metric to select LODs, we never need LODs with error>1 as these should not be selected if the mesh is visible.

The mechanics of LOD selection do not change: when the specific per-LOD error (distance) value at the distance from the camera that the mesh renders from crosses the threshold, the LOD switches. It's configured the same way as before (LOD bias et al work the same way). When the mesh has very smooth normals and no vertex colors, the resulting LOD switch behavior is similar. When the mesh has significant normal variance, the error is typically going to be larger and the LODs will switch a little later - yielding better (and hopefully more uniform) quality at more triangles rendered. When the mesh has vertex colors, with this change the LOD selection should mostly preserve them visually, which didn't happen before.

I'm calling out normal behavior separately from vertex color, although they are functionally the same from the simplification point of view - but previously, the combination of a higher normal weight and the fact that in areas of high normal variance it's typical to also have high positional curvature which translates to higher positional error, the distance-based selection could work okay. However, vertex colors are completely uncorrelated from positions, and in general the combined error is the only "perceptually correct" metric to use here because we don't just care about the silhouettes - we care about the entire appearance.

The default normal merge angle in Blender for "smooth by angle" modifier is 30 degrees; however, since we don't know the intent of the user (are normals flat shaded on purpose? how important is lighting to the look?), I adjusted it to be slightly more conservative; this is just the default and can be changed if necessary per mesh, or globally in the future if we decide 20 is not the best value. 

This change is standalone/self-sufficient. I was considering splitting it into different PRs (e.g. technically we could change the defaults for merge angle separately), but I felt more comfortable doing the whole thing at once as every parameter here changes behavior a little bit and it's easier to test in unison. If issues are found, this can be easily reverted.

Future work includes:

- With this it's now possible to experiment with some sort of attribute addition to solve skinning use cases; areas with high variance of bone influences could be treated as an attribute which would adjust both simplification behavior and LOD switching behavior, which wasn't possible before.
- Normal/color weights could be adjusted in the future and/or made tunable if need be
- This is not new as of this PR, but a general downside of the current simplification logic is that it may in some cases create LODs that have a discontinuous error curve: because the process is guided by triangle counts alone (fixed max error value for all levels), we might create a LOD with error 1e-2, and a next LOD with error 1e-1 at half the triangles, even if we could create (hypothetically) a LOD with error 2e-2 at 75% of the triangles. Changing the logic for how to create each subsequent LOD would improve that and make LOD selection more gradual in certain cases, as well as give us an opportunity to reduce the time it takes to generate LODs.
